description: Baseline, unmodified model.py/train.py: black-box 1-layer LSTM (n_hidden_states=64, hidden_sizes=[64], direct_feedthrough=True), 6-fold leave-one-realization-out CV, 1800s/fold budget, max_epochs=3000.

HYSTERESIS_LFR default config (n_complex_modes=3, n_real_modes=2, hidden_sizes=[32,32]), same training loop as run01 (window_min_length=1000, eval_every=25). Not a divergence/scaling bug -- the derived a_coef/b_coef discretization checked out (stable magnitude<1, target trace/det preserved). Root cause: full-length (16284-sample) eval over 18 sequences every 25 epochs vastly outweighs one training step (4 windows), so only ~75 epochs completed within the 1800s/fold budget -- severe undertraining, not collapse (val stuck near 1.0 but slowly, monotonically improving). Added window_min_length_override + raised eval_every to train.py for a fair retry.

HYSTERESIS_LFR retry with window_min_length_override=250 and eval_every=300. Worse than run02, not better: window_min_length only sets a floor (max stays ~full-sequence length), so per-step cost barely changed; measured directly (~0.0007s/timestep), average window ~3-6k samples costs 10-20s/step. Raising eval_every to 300 backfired -- the fold never reached epoch 300 within budget, so no eval after epoch 1 ever ran, discarding all further training (best_epoch stuck at 1 on every fold). Root-caused with a real timing script this time rather than guessing. Fix for run04: added a genuine window_max_length_override (crops from the window start, matching where y0 is valid) and reverted eval_every to 25.

HYSTERESIS_LFR with window_max_length_override=800 (window_min_length_override=250), eval_every=25. Fixed the throughput bug: now reaches ~350 epochs/17 evals within the 1800s budget (vs run02/03 stuck at 75/1). Genuinely learning now -- train_rmse decreases smoothly and monotonically (0.9962->0.9933 over 350 epochs, no freeze/collapse) -- but far too slowly to be competitive with the LSTM baseline (0.4765) in this budget. Not a bug this time, just a slow learner as configured. Next: try a higher learning rate before writing off the family (lr=1e-3 may be too conservative for this modal parameterization); meanwhile also test other black-box recurrent families (GRU) since explore-then-refine calls for several families before refining.

Black-box GRU (n_hidden_states=64, hidden_sizes=[64], direct_feedthrough=True), otherwise identical to run01 LSTM. Trains cleanly (no collapse, early-stopped at median epoch 362) but clearly worse than LSTM (0.6674 vs 0.4765) on this FSM benchmark -- a different outcome from an unrelated ParallelWH benchmark project noted in this repo's pre-reset history, which is not evidence for this one. LSTM remains the best black-box family so far. Next: settle whether HYSTERESIS_LFR (run04, 0.9933) is lr-limited or fundamentally too slow -- retry with lr=5e-3.

HYSTERESIS_LFR, same as run04 but lr=5e-3 (up from 1e-3). Only marginal improvement at the same epoch budget (0.9829 vs run04's 0.9933 at matched median epoch 350) -- confirms this is NOT primarily an lr issue, the modal/hysteresis parameterization converges slowly regardless. 3 honest attempts (run02/04/06) now point the same way: this architecture, as currently structured (3 complex + 2 real modes, Bouc-Wen hysteresis, this training loop), is not competitive with LSTM inside the fixed 1800s/fold budget. Setting aside for now rather than continuing to tune it; will revisit with a major structural change (e.g. a black-box correction term) if black-box refinement plateaus.

Black-box vanilla RNN (tanh), otherwise identical to run01 LSTM. Trains cleanly (best_epoch median 1112, no collapse) -- 0.5326, between LSTM (0.4765, best) and GRU (0.6674). Completes the black-box recurrent family sweep: LSTM > RNN > GRU on this benchmark. LSTM remains the strongest family overall (also well ahead of HYSTERESIS_LFR's ~0.98-1.0). Next: refine LSTM via moderate hyperparameter changes, starting with n_hidden_states=128 (up from 64).

LSTM refinement: n_hidden_states=128 (up from run01's 64), otherwise identical. Slightly worse than run01 (0.4972 vs 0.4765) at a similar median best_epoch (1125 vs run01's 2000) -- more hidden capacity is not the bottleneck, possibly mild overfitting/harder optimization landscape from the extra parameters. Reverting to n_hidden_states=64. Next: try crops_per_step=8 (up from 4) for smoother gradients.

LSTM, crops_per_step=8 (up from run01's 4), n_hidden_states reverted to 64. Worse than run01 (0.5585 vs 0.4765) -- each step costs ~2x as long, so within the fixed 1800s budget median best_epoch dropped to 1037 (from run01's 2000); more gradient averaging is not worth the reduced step count here. Next: try crops_per_step=2 (fewer windows/step, more steps) as the opposite direction.

LSTM, crops_per_step=2 (down from run01's 4). Worse than run01 (0.4931 vs 0.4765) and hit max_epochs=3000 itself (still improving, not early-stopped/time-capped) -- cheaper but noisier per-step gradient needs more steps just to reach a worse optimum than run01's crops=4 (which early-stopped at epoch 2000 already better). Confirms crops_per_step=4 (the original baseline) is the local optimum among {2,4,8} tested. Next: num_layers=2 (deeper LSTM), a different lever.

LSTM, num_layers=2 (up from run01's 1), crops_per_step reverted to 4. Worse than run01 (0.5540 vs 0.4765) -- each step is more expensive with 2 layers, median best_epoch dropped to 912 (from 2000), same pattern as the capacity/crops sweeps: this model is step-count-limited within budget, and extra capacity/depth costs steps without earning enough back. Reverting to num_layers=1. Next: lr=2e-3 (up from 1e-3) to test if faster convergence closes the gap given the step-count sensitivity just observed.

LSTM, lr=2e-3 (up from run01's 1e-3), num_layers back to 1, crops_per_step=4. First improvement since the baseline: 0.4671 vs run01's 0.4765. Median best_epoch 1800 (vs run01's 2000), so it converges to a better optimum in about the same number of steps -- faster convergence per step, not more steps, is the win here. Confirms the earlier step-count-sensitivity finding (run08/09/11): since capacity increases keep losing to their own higher step cost, pushing convergence speed via lr is the more promising lever. Next: lr=3e-3, one more step in this direction.

LSTM, lr=3e-3 (up from run12's 2e-3). Further improvement: 0.4558 vs run12's 0.4671, at a similar median best_epoch (1900 vs 1800) -- lr trend continues to help. Next: lr=5e-3, one more step before checking for diminishing returns/instability.

LSTM, lr=5e-3 (up from run13's 3e-3). Marginal improvement: 0.4548 vs 0.4558 (~0.2%) -- the lr trend is clearly flattening out. Next: lr=1e-2 to probe whether this is a genuine plateau or the edge before instability, before settling the lr search.

LSTM, lr=1e-2 (up from run14's 5e-3). Statistically identical to run14 (0.4548 vs 0.4548) -- confirms a genuine plateau, not just diminishing returns. Settling the lr search at run14's lr=5e-3 (best_kept). 15-iteration minimum reached; before concluding, trying one major structural modification per PROGRAM.md (hybrid physical+black-box model) since LSTM-family refinement has plateaued.

Hybrid model (new model.py class FSMHybridLFRResidualModel): HYSTERESIS_LFR physical core + a small zero-initialized black-box LSTM residual correction added on top of its output (residual_hidden_size=16), same window caps as the standalone LFR runs (max 800 samples/window, eval_every=25). Substantially better than the pure physical core (0.7750 vs run06's 0.9829) -- confirms the residual correction genuinely helps and the hybrid concept works -- but still far behind the pure black-box LSTM (0.4548). Root cause is the same one throughout the LFR-family runs: the physical core's sequential per-timestep Python loop still gates window size/epoch count (median best_epoch only 325, same ballpark as standalone LFR), and that throughput ceiling outweighs whatever benefit the physical structure adds. Concluding the search: LSTM lr=5e-3 (run14) remains the best model.

Final reported result: test.py --checkpoint-set best_so_far on run14's winning checkpoints (LSTM, lr=5e-3, n_hidden_states=64, hidden_sizes=[64], direct_feedthrough=True, crops_per_step=4). 16 iterations run (exceeds the 15-iteration minimum): explored LSTM/GRU/RNN black-box families and HYSTERESIS_LFR/hybrid physical families (7 meaningfully-different-family runs), refined LSTM via capacity/depth/crops_per_step (all hurt -- step-count-limited within the fixed 1800s/fold budget) and learning rate (helped, then plateaued: run12/13/14 improving, run15 confirming the plateau), then one major structural modification (physical+black-box hybrid, run16) which improved substantially over the pure physical core but still fell well short of the pure LSTM due to the physical core's inherent per-timestep throughput ceiling. model.py/train.py restored to this winning LSTM configuration.
